title: Torsion subsheaf, torsion quotient and generic rank
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field], and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ is torsion if its restriction vanishes on some dense open subset of $U$. The torsion subsheaf $\mathcal T(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal F$ consists of these sections; equivalently, on this integral scheme it is the kernel of the germ map to the generic stalk $\mathcal F_\eta$. Define $\mathcal F/\mathcal T(\mathcal F)$ as the cokernel of its inclusion. Define the generic rank $\operatorname{rk}(\mathcal F)=\dim_K\mathcal F_\eta\in\mathbf N$ when this stalk is finite dimensional, with value $0$ for infinite dimensional generic stalks.
